---
title: "Lab 04 — Mixed models in R"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(lme4)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
sleep <- read.csv("data/sleepstudy.csv")
sleep$Subject <- factor(sleep$Subject)
cbpp <- read.csv("data/cbpp.csv")
cbpp$herd   <- factor(cbpp$herd)
cbpp$period <- factor(cbpp$period)
fit_cp  <- lm(Reaction ~ Days, data = sleep)
fit_ri  <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleep)
fit_pp  <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleep)
fit_glm <- glm(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period, family = binomial, data = cbpp)
fit_lap <- glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),
                 family = binomial, data = cbpp)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab04", title = "Mixed models in R", open = "q10")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1  = "The ICC of the random-intercept model Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject) is about…",
  q2  = "In Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), the estimated SD of the random slopes is 5.92 ms/day. This means…",
  q3  = "The standard error of the Days slope is 1.24 from lm() and 1.55 from lmer(). Which statement is right?",
  q4  = "Which comparison must be made with ML fits (REML = FALSE)?",
  q5  = "The LRT of (Days | Subject) against (1 | Subject) gives T = 42.8. The correct reference distribution is…",
  q6  = "In the random-intercept model (n_i = 10 for every subject) the BLUP of each subject equals its raw deviation times…",
  q7  = "After keeping only Days 0-1 for subjects 308, 309 and 310 and refitting the random-intercept model, the shrinkage factor for those subjects is about…",
  q8  = "In the cbpp GLMM, exp(beta_period2) = 0.37. The right interpretation is…",
  q9  = "Laplace (nAGQ = 1) gives sd_herd = 0.642 and nAGQ = 25 gives 0.648. What do you conclude?",
  q10 = "In cbpp, the period-1 probability of a new case is 0.198 for a typical herd (b = 0) and 0.216 averaged over herds. Explain the difference and say which one you would report to a ministry planning vaccine supplies."
)
```

## What you will do

Fit linear mixed models to `sleepstudy` and a binomial GLMM to `cbpp`, then answer the questions. The data and the models `fit_cp`, `fit_ri`, `fit_pp`, `fit_glm` and `fit_lap` are already loaded in every exercise box. Then download the `.txt`.

## Linear mixed models

Compute the ICC of the random-intercept model.

```{r icc-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=4}
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit_ri))
vc
vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("0.59: about 59% of the variance (given Days) is between subjects, and two measurements of the same subject have correlation 0.59.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.41: the share of the variance that is within subjects is the ICC."),
  answer("0.07: the correlation between intercepts and slopes."),
  answer("0.94: the shrinkage factor of the BLUPs."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Subjects differ in how fast they deteriorate: about 95% have a slope between roughly -1 and 22 ms per day.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The average slope 10.47 is estimated with standard error 5.92."),
  answer("Reaction times scatter with SD 5.92 ms around each subject's own line."),
  answer("Each subject's own lm() slope has standard error 5.92."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("1.55 is right: lm() treats 180 correlated rows as independent, and ignores that slopes vary between the 18 subjects.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("1.24 is right: lm() uses all 180 observations, so it is more efficient."),
  answer("Both are right: the point estimates are equal, so the standard errors do not matter."),
  answer("1.55 is right because REML always gives larger standard errors than least squares."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

Test the random slope against the random-intercept model.

```{r slope-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
a <- anova(fit_ri, fit_pp, refit = FALSE)
a
T <- a$Chisq[2]
0.5 * pchisq(T, 1, lower.tail = FALSE) + 0.5 * pchisq(T, 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

```{r q4}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  answer("Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject) against Reaction ~ 1 + (Days | Subject).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject) against Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)."),
  answer("Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject) against Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)."),
  answer("None: REML likelihoods can always be compared."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("A 50:50 mixture of chi-square(1) and chi-square(2), because the slope variance is 0 on the boundary under H0; p is about 3e-10.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Chi-square with 2 df, as for any LRT with two extra parameters."),
  answer("Chi-square with 1 df, because only one variance is added."),
  answer("No test is possible because the models were fitted with REML."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q6}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  answer("k = 10 sigma_b^2 / (10 sigma_b^2 + sigma^2) = 0.935.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("k = sigma_b^2 / (sigma_b^2 + sigma^2) = 0.589, the ICC."),
  answer("k = 1: BLUPs equal the raw deviations when the design is balanced."),
  answer("k = sigma^2 / (10 sigma_b^2 + sigma^2) = 0.065."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

Refit the random-intercept model with only two observations for three subjects.

```{r shrink-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=7}
s2 <- subset(sleep, !(Subject %in% c("308", "309", "310")) | Days <= 1)
r2 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = s2)
v  <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(r2))$vcov
c(k_2 = 2 * v[1] / (2 * v[1] + v[2]), k_10 = 10 * v[1] / (10 * v[1] + v[2]))
```

```{r q7}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q7"]],
  answer("0.65, against 0.90 for the subjects with ten observations: fewer observations, stronger shrinkage.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.90, the same as for the other subjects: the shrinkage factor does not depend on n_i."),
  answer("0.25: with two observations the BLUP is almost zero."),
  answer("1.00: subjects with few observations are not shrunk."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## A binomial GLMM

```{r glmm-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
exp(fixef(fit_lap))
fit_agq <- update(fit_lap, nAGQ = 25)
c(laplace = attr(VarCorr(fit_lap)$herd, "stddev"),
  agq25   = attr(VarCorr(fit_agq)$herd, "stddev"))
```

```{r q8}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q8"]],
  answer("For a given herd, the odds of a new case in period 2 are 0.37 times the odds in period 1.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Across all herds, the proportion of new cases in period 2 is 37% of that in period 1."),
  answer("The probability of a new case in period 2 is 0.37."),
  answer("Herds differ in their odds by a factor 0.37."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q9}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q9"]],
  answer("The Laplace approximation is accurate for these data; quadrature changes the estimates only in the third decimal.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Laplace is wrong: always use the largest nAGQ and compare logLik values across nAGQ."),
  answer("The herd variance is not significant because the two values differ."),
  answer("nAGQ = 25 gives the REML estimate."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q10}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q10"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "The GLMM coefficients are conditional on the herd…",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
